description:
client.rs:182-201 — JmapClient::new
client.rs:208-214 — JmapClient::new_plain

Signature: `new(transport: impl TransportConfig, auth: impl AuthProvider + 'static, ...)`

The constructor takes `auth` by value. Then internally wraps it in `Arc::new(auth)` at line 197.

This means a caller cannot:

1. Construct an Arc<BearerAuth> once, then pass clones to multiple JmapClients. Today, each JmapClient gets its OWN Arc wrapping the auth — sharing requires constructing the AuthProvider once and using `Arc::new` outside (which yields `Arc<dyn AuthProvider>`, not the concrete type). For example, a deployment with two JmapClient instances pointing at different shards but using the same OAuth token holder cannot share refresh logic — each JmapClient holds its own Arc<dyn AuthProvider>, so a refresh in one is invisible to the other.

2. The `impl AuthProvider + 'static` bound is stricter than necessary. The actual stored type is Arc<dyn AuthProvider>, so the constructor really only needs `auth: Arc<dyn AuthProvider>` — or alternatively, an `Into<Arc<dyn AuthProvider>>` bound that accepts either a bare impl or a pre-existing Arc.

This is a defensive-code-forcing pattern: every caller who wants shared auth has to first construct their own Arc<MyAuthProvider> and then pass it to new(). The `Arc<dyn AuthProvider>` blanket impl (auth.rs:288-292) exists to support this pattern but the foundation constructor doesn't expose it cleanly.

Recommendation: in the next minor release, add a constructor variant `JmapClient::new_with_shared_auth(transport, auth: Arc<dyn AuthProvider>, base_url, config)` that takes the Arc by value. Existing new() stays as the ergonomic case for callers with a fresh auth provider.
title: JmapClient::new and new_plain take owned auth/transport — no way to clone or share auth across clients
